subject: Reserved capacity exception & SKU rebalance request — ArgusAI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Argus capacity ask — pricing sensitivity and exception runway

Team — forwarding the request from Argus (below). Key asks: 12-month reserved capacity (phased activation) with a two-way SKU rebalance option at month 6, and a price-protection clause if spot GPU costs move >25% vs. today. They are pushing for a 25% discount off list for the initial 12-month commit and want the discount to be triggered into contract language and billing.

Quick notes / ask:
- I attached high-level scenarios (argus_capacity_scenarios.xlsx) that map their wanted SKU mix to our GPU pool.
- If we give >20% discount we need exec approval and finance sign-off on exposure caps.
- SKU rebalance at month 6 is operationally doable but requires a buffer in the reserved bucket and a fallback policy to avoid latency slippage.

Can Karthik and Laura estimate the P&L exposure (net of expected burst usage) and list the approval path for anything >20%? Sean — can you lead the customer conversation on acceptable fallbacks (graceful degradation triggers) and timeline for DocuSign?

Thanks,

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- argus_capacity_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Argus capacity ask — pricing sensitivity and exception runway

Agree with Marissa. Quick add from finance ops perspective:
- We ran three price-shock scenarios (see the modeled tabs in the spreadsheet): baseline, +30% GPU cost, +60% GPU cost. With their proposed SKU mix and 12-month tenor, a 25% off-list discount would push EBITDA-negative for the reserved tranche under the +30% scenario unless we include a GPU-cost pass-through or indexed floor.
- Approval thresholds: discounts <=15% are sales-managed; 15–20% require VP Sales sign-off + Finance attestation; >20% requires Exec (CRO/CEO) sign-off and a contingency escrow or crediting mechanism.
- Operational asks: if we accept a rebalance at month 6 we must reserve a 10% buffer in the fleet for burst to avoid SLA violations during rebalancing windows. That buffer can be priced in as an optional add-on.

I'll prepare a short memo for execs (2 slides) summarizing exposure and suggested guardrails. Laura — can you confirm whether Legal will accept an indexation clause referencing a public GPU spot index or whether we need a vendor-signed cost statement?

Karthik
Head of Deal Structuring | Redwood Inference
From: Beth Langston <beth.langston@argusai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity request — ArgusAI SOW v2

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. We updated the SOW to reflect a 12-month initial commit with a month-6 SKU rebalance option and included a proposed price-protection clause (attached: Argus_SOW_v2.pdf). Our commercial team is pushing for a 25% off-list concession to make the economics work for our board this quarter — they want the discount written into the main contract (not as a separate rebate).

We understand you may need guardrails. Two acceptable alternatives for us if discount approval is limited:
1) Indexation: apply the discount but allow a trigger that re-prices if a public GPU index increases by >30% for two rolling months.
2) Credit escrow: keep the discount but cap Redwood's exposure to X USD per quarter, with excess credited back to us or applied as future credits.

We can go to DocuSign as soon as pricing is finalized. Can you let us know the maximum concession you can offer without exec sign-off?

Thanks — Beth
Beth Langston | VP, Operations | ArgusAI
Attachments:
- Argus_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Langston <beth.langston@argusai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity request — ArgusAI SOW v2

Beth — thanks for the update and the clearer asks. We like option (1) indexation as the primary path because it preserves predictability for both sides while protecting Redwood from sustained GPU cost shocks. Proposal from our side:

- Initial commercial: 15% off list for the 12-month reserved tranche (applies to baseline SKU mix).
- Indexed protection: If a mutually-agreed GPU supply index rises >25% for two consecutive months, pricing reverts to list minus 5% (i.e., temporary pause of the concession) or we implement a phased unwind over a 30-day notice.
- SKU rebalance at month 6: permitted once, subject to a 10% buffer reservation and a single rebalance fee to cover re-provisioning risk.
- If Argus requires the 25% concession written as firm contract language we will need Exec approval; we can move that request to our CRO with a one-page exposure memo and Finance scenarios.

Attached is an initial proposal (pricing_proposal_argus_v1.pdf). Sean will follow up to align on operational fallbacks and the DocuSign timeline.

Appreciate the openness — let us know which index you prefer and whether Argus can accept the 10% buffer as an optional add-on.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments:
- pricing_proposal_argus_v1.pdf (pdf)
